answer: At the onyx‑secured summit of the network, each agent registers a cryptographic vault that timestamps all payments and stores a unique hardware fingerprint. The grove protocol links any identities that ever share a vault, source or identical timing pattern into a single kin‑node, forcing the ledger to treat them as one. An attacker must duplicate the hardware fingerprint and create independent, untimed vaults for every fake node, raising cost linearly with the number of Sybil identities.
